result.verdict: SignalGate is a genuinely differentiated wedge — execution discipline and an auditable ledger for signal followers, in a category drowning in scams — and the engineering honesty is a real asset. But the site's two headline claims (executes "even when you're not watching"; "reads your channel the moment it lands") are contradicted by the actual mechanism (mandatory YES tap, 5-minute expiry, no channel ingestion, gold-only parser), and the centerpiece proof (the verified record) has no plan anywhere to be generated. The product is closer to sellable than the messaging is to honest, which is exactly backwards for a brand whose entire pitch is honesty.

findings.title: Hero promise contradicts the core mechanism: nothing executes when you're not watching
findings.finding: The hero H1 sells absent-execution — 'The signals you follow, executed properly — even when you're not watching' (site-2-editorial-transparency.html:344) — but the system requires a YES tap on every trade and signals expire after 5 minutes (site lines 468, 720: 'Cards wait for you and expire after 5 minutes if untouched — a missed card is simply no trade'; .env.example DEFAULT_SIGNAL_EXPIRY_MINUTES=5). While the buyer is asleep or driving — the exact scenarios the problem section invokes — the product does nothing.
findings.evidence: site-mockups/site-2-editorial-transparency.html:344 ('even when you're not watching'), :468 ('A signal expires after 5 minutes'), :720 (FAQ admits missed card = no trade); docs/ARCHITECTURE.md 'A human approves each signal'
findings.why_it_matters: The buyer discovers the contradiction inside the same page (hero vs FAQ) and reads it as bait-and-switch — fatal for a product whose entire differentiator is honesty. It also sets up churn: the ICP's #1 pain (missed entries while away) is not solved, only made safe.
findings.fix: Reframe the hero to the discipline promise the product actually keeps — the copy deck's default H1 ('executed by the rulebook — in one tap. A hard stop every time') is already better. Position 'missed card = no trade' as a guardrail feature, not hide it. Do NOT solve this with auto-copy.

findings.title: 'How it works' step 1 claims channel ingestion that does not exist in the code
findings.finding: Step 1 says 'A signal posts in your channel. SignalGate reads it the moment it lands' (site line 409). There is no Telegram channel listener anywhere: the bot's only message handlers are commands, provider photo/document uploads, and provider text (telegram_bot/bot.py:51-57). Signals enter only via admin /testsignal, POST /signals/create, or the invite-coded provider screenshot flow. A prospect connecting 'their channel' cannot.
findings.evidence: site-mockups/site-2-editorial-transparency.html:409; telegram_bot/bot.py:51-57 (MessageHandler filters.PHOTO / Document.IMAGE / TEXT only — no channel_post handler); docs/ARCHITECTURE.md flow starts at 'Admin issues /testsignal'
findings.why_it_matters: This is a 'claimed but not substantiated' capability on the page's most load-bearing section. First real prospect who asks 'how do I connect my channel?' exposes it.
findings.fix: Rewrite step 1 to the true mechanism: 'Your signal provider sends the signal (text or screenshot); SignalGate structures it and cards it to you.' Optionally scope channel-forwarding ingestion as a post-pilot feature.

findings.title: Gold-only parser sold as a general 'signals you follow' product
findings.finding: The parser accepts only GOLD/XAU/XAUUSD (backend/app/parser.py:17-20) and rejects everything else ('No recognised symbol', parser.py:98), yet the site pitches generic signals ('symbol, direction, entry, stop, take-profits') and the vision prompt even cites BTCUSD as an example (vision_extractor.py). Any prospect following an FX/crypto/indices channel hits a wall on signal one.
findings.evidence: backend/app/parser.py:17-20,98; site-mockups/site-2-editorial-transparency.html step 2 copy; backend/app/vision_extractor.py EXTRACTION_PROMPT ('e.g. XAUUSD, GOLD, BTCUSD')
findings.why_it_matters: Either the page over-promises or the pilot funnel fills with unusable leads. Gold-only is a fine v1 constraint — as long as it is stated.
findings.fix: State 'XAUUSD/gold signals in v1' on the page and in the demo-request form; make a configurable symbol whitelist the first post-pilot roadmap item.

findings.title: README's 'no AI parsing' claim is now false — the AI screenshot extractor exists
findings.finding: README.md:41 lists '❌ AI / fuzzy signal parsing (deterministic only)' under 'What does NOT exist in v1', but backend/app/vision_extractor.py ships a ClaudeExtractor calling the Anthropic vision API (SIGNAL_EXTRACTOR=claude, auto-selected when ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is present). The internal safety framing is good — AI output feeds the deterministic parser and requires human Confirm — but the headline claim is inaccurate, and README's 'What works in v1' list omits the screenshot/provider flow entirely.
findings.evidence: README.md:41 vs backend/app/vision_extractor.py:1-22,120,220-227; docs/BEN_NEXT_STAGE_CHECKLIST.md §2 ('SIGNAL_EXTRACTOR=claude ... ANTHROPIC_API_KEY')
findings.why_it_matters: For a product whose brand is auditability, the top-level doc misstating what the pipeline contains is self-inflicted damage; a diligent tester (or skeptic) will find it in minutes.
findings.fix: Update README: 'AI is used only to transcribe screenshots into candidate text; the deterministic parser remains the sole validity authority and a human confirms every extraction.' Add the provider flow to 'What works.'

findings.title: The centerpiece proof (verified record) has no generation plan anywhere
findings.finding: The record section is the page's designated proof beat (MESSAGE_MAP.md §6) and is honestly labelled SAMPLE throughout, but none of the strategy docs — HOSTED_VERSION_PLAN.md, docs/BEN_NEXT_STAGE_CHECKLIST.md (screenshot plumbing only), MESSAGE_MAP.md — schedules the forward-test that would produce a real record, even though the product itself is the record-generating machine (performance ledger, R tracking, full audit trail).
findings.evidence: site verification modal: 'the honest state is a demo verification pack rather than a public third-party report'; _copy-deck.md placeholder list ('all performance numbers (sample)'); absence of any forward-test timeline in the three strategy docs
findings.why_it_matters: Every week without a running structured forward-test delays the only asset that makes the page sellable. The proof cannot be bought or written — only accumulated.
findings.fix: Start a defined 60–90 day demo forward-test now: fixed rulebook, every Nick signal carded, ledger exported weekly. Make this the top-priority workstream ahead of hosting, pricing, or more site work.

findings.title: Two ICPs are conflated; the built product points at providers, the site sells to followers
findings.finding: MESSAGE_MAP.md defines the buyer as 'a retail trader who already follows signals,' but everything actually built and operationalized is provider-led: invite-coded provider role, screenshot ingestion, broadcast-to-testers, the 'Signal desk' plan card, and the entire Nick workflow (MESSAGE_TO_NICK.md, NICK_SCREENSHOT_PROVIDER_GUIDE.md). A follower cannot self-serve (no channel ingestion, finding #2); a provider can, today.
findings.evidence: site-mockups/MESSAGE_MAP.md 'Who we're selling to'; docs/MESSAGE_TO_NICK.md; site-2 pricing card 'Signal desk — Private setup: For a signal provider testing approval cards with multiple demo users'
findings.why_it_matters: Provider-led is also the better GTM: one provider brings N followers (built-in distribution), wants the verified record as their own credibility asset, and absorbs the setup friction the hosted plan worries about.
findings.fix: Make the signal provider the primary pilot customer (B2B2C); sell followers through providers. Keep the follower page as the eventual end-state, clearly marked.

findings.title: The user's own execution record — the product's key asset — has no user-facing surface
findings.finding: Testers approve trades and receive lifecycle pings, but the ledger and command history are admin-only (/lastsignals, /lastcommands are admin commands per README.md:25-26; admin endpoints require X-Admin-Id per docs/ARCHITECTURE.md). The tester never sees 'your record': approvals, R outcomes, discipline stats.
findings.evidence: README.md:25-26 ('admin /testsignal, /pause, /resume, /users, /lastsignals, /lastcommands'); docs/ARCHITECTURE.md Auth section
findings.why_it_matters: The retention loop and the differentiator vs every signal channel is 'here is your audited execution record.' Without a user surface, the product feels like a remote-control button, not a discipline tool.
findings.fix: Add a /myrecord bot command and/or a weekly ledger digest per tester — the data already exists in performance_ledger.

findings.title: Problem section sells position-sizing discipline v1 does not provide
findings.finding: The problem copy names 'You size it on a feeling' / 'Wrong size, moved stops' as pains the product fixes, but v1 has no per-user sizing logic: lots are fixed demo constants (0.01/0.02 split-ticket) and users.risk_percent is a nullable field with no consuming logic in the approval→command path.
findings.evidence: _copy-deck.md §2 ('You size it on a feeling'); site-2 pains list '03 Wrong size, moved stops'; CLAUDE.md schema (risk_percent nullable, fixed_lot_size default 0.01); README.md split-ticket table
findings.why_it_matters: Fixed demo lots technically remove 'sizing on a feeling,' but a live-minded buyer will read this as risk-based sizing, which doesn't exist. Small over-claim, on-brand-damaging.
findings.fix: Soften to 'a fixed, pre-set size — never a feeling' in v1 copy; scope risk-percent sizing as a post-pilot feature.

findings.title: 5-minute expiry is safe but likely starves the usage loop for the stated ICP; measure, don't guess
findings.finding: The default 5-minute expiry (a good anti-stale guardrail) combined with mandatory approval means a busy follower will let most cards expire, so the ICP experiences 'no trades' rather than 'disciplined trades.' No doc plans to measure card→approval conversion or considers provider-set expiry per signal type (e.g., longer for limit entries).
findings.evidence: .env.example DEFAULT_SIGNAL_EXPIRY_MINUTES=5; site line 720; no expiry-tuning discussion in HOSTED_VERSION_PLAN.md or MESSAGE_MAP.md (unverified assumption re: actual approval rates — no usage data exists yet)
findings.why_it_matters: If 90% of cards expire, the pilot 'fails' for the wrong reason. The fix is a tunable, still-bounded parameter plus instrumentation — not weakening approval.
findings.fix: Instrument card-sent→decision rate in the pilot; allow the provider to set expiry per signal within a hard cap (e.g., 5–60 min for limit orders). Keep human approval untouched.

findings.title: No defined pilot offer behind the 'Request Pilot' CTA
findings.finding: The pricing section honestly avoids fake prices (good), but 'Pilot — Invite access' and 'Signal desk — Private setup' have no defined contents anywhere: no duration, deliverables, success criteria, or expectations doc. The demo-request form collects leads into a jsonl with no follow-up artifact to send them.
findings.evidence: site-2 pricing cards ('Guided setup for one tester...', 'Request Pilot'); _copy-deck.md §8 all-placeholder plans; no pilot-definition doc in docs/
findings.why_it_matters: Real pricing is correctly out of scope, but an undefined pilot means every inbound lead gets an improvised, inconsistent experience — and you can't learn from a pilot with no success criteria.
findings.fix: Write a one-page pilot definition (see deliverables §6): who, duration, what they get, what you measure, exit criteria. Free is fine; defined is mandatory.

result.deliverables:
# Expert 1 — Product Strategist: Deliverables

## 1. One-sentence positioning
**SignalGate is demo-first execution discipline for signal traders: every signal from your provider becomes a structured, hard-stopped, one-tap trade card, and every outcome — losses included — lands in an auditable record you (and your followers) can check.**

## 2. Strongest current value proposition
The **deterministic boundary + audit trail**, working end-to-end today: raw Telegram text never reaches MetaTrader; only a parsed, validated, human-approved, one-time-only command does — with a hard stop on every trade, idempotent approvals, expiry, pause, and a full lifecycle ledger (50/50 tests passing). In a category defined by black boxes and screenshot "proof," a system that can show its own receipts is the moat. The anti-scam contrast section of the site is not marketing spin — the code substantiates it. That is rare and worth protecting above all else.

## 3. Weakest current product assumption
**That the buyer's problem is solved by safe approval rather than by presence.** The messaging assumes a follower who misses entries "while asleep or driving" will be satisfied that a missed card is "simply no trade." That's a guardrail, not the job-to-be-done. The honest v1 job is *"when I DO act, I act by the rulebook, and I get a record proving it"* — a real and sellable job, but a different one from "never miss a signal again," which is what the hero currently sells (site-2:344) and the product cannot deliver without abandoning human approval (which it must not). Second-weakest: that a follower can self-serve at all — with no channel ingestion and a gold-only parser, v1 is operationally a provider-distributed tool.

## 4. Highest-value offer upgrades (ranked)
1. **The Verified Record as a product ("Provider Proof Pack")** — run the 60–90 day structured demo forward-test, export the ledger weekly, and package it as the signal provider's own third-party-checkable track record. Rationale: it monetizes the ledger you already built, it's the asset every honest provider lacks, and it generates the site's proof section as a by-product. Zero new safety surface.
2. **Personal execution record for followers (/myrecord + weekly digest)** — surfaces existing performance_ledger data per user. Rationale: cheapest build with the biggest retention effect; turns the product from a remote-control into a discipline mirror ("your approval rate, your R, your record").
3. **Hosted onboarding (per HOSTED_VERSION_PLAN.md)** — one server, one shared bot, license keys; customer keeps only MT5. Rationale: the plan is sound and honest about the MT5-VPS catch; it's the prerequisite for charging anyone, but it should follow — not precede — the forward-test record.
4. **Symbol whitelist expansion (config-driven, still deterministic)** — unlocks non-gold providers. Rationale: widens the funnel materially at low parser risk; keep the same rejection-first validation per symbol.
5. **Provider-set expiry within a hard cap + conversion instrumentation** — fixes the likely expiry-starvation problem with data, not vibes.
*Deliberately NOT upgrades:* live trading, auto-copy, trailing stops, payments — correctly excluded from v1; live remains a separate, legal-reviewed, deliberate future decision (HOSTED_VERSION_PLAN.md's two flags are right).

## 5. Sharpest ICP
**Primary (pilot): the small, honest signal provider — "Nick."** Runs a gold-focused Telegram signal channel with 50–2,000 followers; posts screenshots or text calls; has no verifiable track record and knows the scam stigma costs him subscribers; technically average (can install MT5, won't run Python). He wants: (a) his calls executed consistently by followers so his signal quality is judged fairly, and (b) a read-only, losses-included record he can point to. He brings distribution — every provider onboards his own followers as testers.
**Secondary (through the provider): the disciplined follower.** Already pays for or follows a signal channel, has an MT5 demo, has been burned by his own late fills and moved stops, is scam-wary. He is the site's current addressee — right person, wrong stage. Sell to him via his provider, not cold.

## 6. First sellable pilot contents ("Pilot" behind the site CTA — define it, price it free)
- **Who:** 1 signal provider (Nick archetype) + 3–5 of their real followers as testers. Invite-only.
- **Duration:** 8 weeks fixed, with a stated goal: *produce the first real demo execution record.*
- **What's included:**
  1. Provider setup: invite code, screenshot flow (per BEN_NEXT_STAGE_CHECKLIST.md), guided walkthrough, honest disclosure of the AI-transcription step.
  2. Tester setup: Telegram registration + choice of (a) own MT5 demo with the EA, or (b) simulator/operator-run shared MT5 demo terminal — so a tester can participate with *Telegram only*, collapsing onboarding to one tap. (Demo-only makes a shared terminal safe; it also pre-tests the hosted model.)
  3. Weekly ledger export to provider and testers (upgrade #2 in minimal form — even a formatted Telegram message).
  4. Ops: gold-only, 5-min default expiry (provider may request per-signal expiry up to a capped max if instrumented), admin pause drill in week 1.
- **What you measure (success criteria):** cards sent → decision rate; approval → execution success rate; % cards expired; parser/extraction rejection rate; count of safety-rule triggers (dupes blocked, expired blocked); provider willingness-to-pay interview at week 8.
- **Explicit exclusions (stated in the pilot doc):** no live accounts, no payments, no auto-copy, no non-gold symbols, no profit expectations — testers sign the same demo-only acknowledgment the site form already contains.
- **Exit:** a published demo verification pack replacing the site's SAMPLE data, and a go/no-go on the hosted build.

**Pre-pilot must-fix list (from findings):** hero reframe (F1), step-1 copy truth (F2), gold-only disclosure (F3), README AI-extraction correction (F4), pilot definition doc (F10).

Gating is genuinely strong: the model only transcribes text to a candidate string, the deterministic parser remains sole validity authority (vision_extractor.py:1-14), a human provider must Confirm before broadcast, and extraction is audited (SIGNAL_IMAGE_EXTRACTED). But it is a real scope expansion and README.md:41 still denies it exists — the spec/README should be amended to describe the gate rather than pretend the feature is absent. Live Claude-engine path unverified (no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY here); FakeExtractor path verified by tests.

rows.evidence: crud.py:174-242 (generate_license_key, issue_license, resolve_ea_user with hosted-vs-local logic), config.py:82 REQUIRE_LICENSE default false, unique license_key column (models.py:43-45), admin endpoints admin.py:64-100, /commands/pending resolves by license (commands.py:88-99). 6 passing tests incl. test_require_license_mode_rejects_userid_only and test_deactivated_customer_gets_no_command (tests/test_licensing.py).

rows.evidence: Code-side support is real and tested: postgres:// URL normalization (config.py:56-60), backend/requirements-hosted.txt adds psycopg2-binary, REQUIRE_LICENSE mode. Deployment itself is documentation only: HOSTED_DEPLOYMENT.md (VPS/Caddy/Postgres runbook, honest 'demo-only posture unchanged' + regulation note) and WINDOWS_VPS_SETUP.md (single-box 2-week solo test plan). No server exists, nothing is deployed.
rows.notes: Docs are plans, and they say so — no false 'we are hosted' claim found. The Postgres path has never been exercised against a real Postgres in this repo (tests run SQLite) — mark the Postgres migration Needs verification before any VPS pilot. Public cloud deployment itself stays outside v1 scope; the docs are the right prep.

rows.area: Demo site (3 mockups + primary) and site_server.py form capture
rows.evidence: site-mockups/site-1-quant-desk.html (46KB), site-2-editorial-transparency.html (61KB, primary — site_server.py:70 prints its URL as the landing target; orchestrator confirmed HTTP 200), site-3-verified-accountable.html (49KB). site_server.py:21-53 validates the 6 required fields on POST /api/demo-requests and appends to demo-requests.jsonl (gitignored; orchestrator verified the endpoint works). MESSAGE_MAP.md + _copy-deck.md define the message spine.
rows.notes: Local mockups only — no deployment, no real CRM/email (correctly outside v1 scope; form capture to jsonl is the honest placeholder). demo-requests.jsonl does not exist yet (created on first submission).

rows.area: Site claims vs repo reality (verification feed, track record, pricing, identity)
rows.evidence: site-2 line 560: 'Reconciled trade-by-trade from a read-only broker connection — not screenshots, not our word' and line 353 'Independently reconciled record — read-only audit (sample)'; 'Demo verification pack · report SG-DEMO-2026-08 · account DEMO-000 · 168 trades · SAMPLE' (561); 'Win rate 56% · Profit factor 1.42' (514-515). NO read-only broker connection, verification pack, reconciliation process, or 168-trade record exists anywhere in the repo.
rows.notes: Heavily mitigated: every figure carries SAMPLE labels (25/21/12+ 'sample' occurrences per file), the banner says 'replace each figure with verified numbers before publishing' (507), the verification modal admits 'the numbers shown on this demo page are still sample data' (765), pricing is Free/Invite/Private with no fake prices (586-598), and identity is a placeholder 'SG DEMO' portrait, not a fake person (568-575). Residual risk: the MECHANISM claims ('read-only broker connection', 'independently reconciled') read as describing an existing process, not a sample figure — before any real prospect sees this, either build the demo verification pack from the actual performance_ledger or reword to 'will be reconciled'. This is exactly the north-star fix: generate the pack from the ledger you actually have.

rows.evidence: direction-1/2/3-*.html (16-19KB each) are earlier visual-direction drafts of the same three concepts superseded by the full site-1/2/3 pages (46-61KB); all six are git-tracked (git ls-files). backend/signalgate.db exists on disk but is correctly gitignored (*.db, signalgate.db in .gitignore); demo-requests.jsonl and provider_ids.json also gitignored.
rows.notes: Not defects, but the direction-* drafts should be moved to an archive/ folder or deleted before sharing the repo with a prospect/tester — a visitor opening the folder cannot tell which page is canonical (MESSAGE_MAP.md references 'the chosen visual direction' without naming site-2 as the pick; only site_server.py:70 does).

result.notes: CROSS-CUTTING OBSERVATIONS (inventory agent). 1) The build substantially EXCEEDS the CLAUDE.md v1 spec in four areas — vision screenshot extraction, signal-provider role, licensing/hosted mode, and the marketing site — while README.md still describes the original spec (line 41 denies AI parsing exists; lines 136-137 describe a broadcast limitation the code no longer has). The single highest-leverage doc fix before showing anyone is a README refresh that owns the vision feature and describes its gates (preview-only, deterministic parser final authority, human Confirm, audit-logged) instead of denying it. 2) Safety spine is genuinely built and tested end-to-end minus MT5: raw text never reaches the EA (parser boundary + serialize_command at commands.py:28-76 is the only EA payload), one-command-per-YES, duplicate/expiry/pause guards all have passing tests. 3) The only spec items I could not verify in this environment are runtime ones: MQL5 compilation/execution (no MT5 on Linux), live Telegram bot behavior (no token), the Claude vision engine (no API key), and Postgres mode (tests run SQLite) — all four are 'works on paper, verify on the Windows box'. 4) The MT5 EA is missing the spec-required client-side COMMAND_EXPIRED check (grep confirms no expiry logic in SignalGateEA.mq5); backend-side filtering makes this defense-in-depth, not exploitable, but it should be added since the spec lists it explicitly. 5) The launchers bind 0.0.0.0 deliberately (cross-machine MT5) while every doc says 127.0.0.1 — document the divergence. 6) The site is unusually honest for this category (SAMPLE labels, no fake prices, no fake identity, real risk warnings at line 739); the one residual claim-vs-reality gap is mechanism language about a 'read-only broker connection / independently reconciled record' that has no repo artifact behind it — the natural fix is to generate a real demo verification pack from the performance_ledger table that already exists. 7) Nothing in the repo recommends live trading, auto-copying, or weakened approval; demo-only defaults are enforced at config (config.py:86), backend (demo_only=True hardcoded in serialize_command line 75), and EA (OnInit refuses live accounts) — three independent layers, all verified in code.

result.verdict: The product's honest core — one-tap approval, hard stops, idempotent commands, a full audit ledger — is genuinely differentiated, but the site sells a different product than the one in the repo: it claims independent reconciliation, channel auto-reading, and away-from-screen execution that do not exist, while the actual sellable assets (the ledger, the Nick screenshot-gatekeeper flow, the guided demo) are underpackaged or invisible. The pricing section has plan cards but no offer: nothing a buyer would pay for is defined, and the one prospective partner (Nick) is handed a task list with zero stated benefit. Fix the four unsubstantiated claims before any prospect sees the page, then rebuild the ladder around what is real: a hosted guided demo, a concierge pilot, and a provider desk whose product is a forward-test record of the provider's own signals.

findings.title: FAQ asserts 'independently reconciled' record as unqualified fact — no such reconciliation exists
findings.finding: The FAQ answer states the performance record is independently reconciled with no SAMPLE qualifier, while the record section itself carries a SAMPLE banner and the proof modal admits the honest state is 'a demo verification pack rather than a public third-party report'.
findings.evidence: site-mockups/site-2-editorial-transparency.html:700 — 'the full record, losses included, is independently reconciled.' Contrast :507 'SAMPLE DATA — replace each figure with verified numbers before publishing' and :765 'the honest state is a demo verification pack rather than a public third-party report.' Hero anchor :353 does carry '(sample)'; the FAQ line does not.
findings.why_it_matters: A fabricated verification claim is the exact scam-tell the page's own 'Why it's different' section attacks (:496 'Read-only, audited record'). One skeptical prospect who clicks the proof modal after reading the FAQ concludes the operator lies, and the entire trust architecture collapses.
findings.fix: Rewrite the FAQ line to 'every trade is logged in an audit ledger you can inspect; independent reconciliation is planned before any live discussion' — or add the same (sample) qualifier used in the hero anchor.

findings.title: 'How it works' step 1 claims automatic channel ingestion that is not built
findings.finding: Step 1 says SignalGate reads signals from the buyer's channel the moment they land. There is no channel-listening code: signal ingestion is admin-typed /testsignal text or a provider-uploaded screenshot.
findings.evidence: site-mockups/site-2-editorial-transparency.html:409 — 'A signal posts in your channel. SignalGate reads it the moment it lands.' telegram_bot/bot.py:33-56 registers only CommandHandlers (/start, /testsignal, etc.), YES/NO callbacks, and PHOTO/Document.IMAGE handlers; grep for 'channel|forward' in telegram_bot/handlers.py returns zero matches.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the first concrete mechanism claim on the page, and any demo tester discovers within minutes that signals arrive via the operator or a screenshot provider, not their own channel. Broken step-1 expectation poisons everything after it.
findings.fix: Rewrite step 1 to what exists: 'Your provider posts the signal (text or screenshot); SignalGate turns it into a checked trade card within seconds.' Keep channel auto-reading as an honest roadmap item.

findings.title: Hero promise 'even when you're not watching' contradicts the product's own 5-minute expiry + mandatory tap
findings.finding: The H1 sells away-from-screen execution, but the mechanic requires the user to tap Approve within 5 minutes or nothing trades — the FAQ itself concedes 'a missed card is simply no trade'.
findings.evidence: site-mockups/site-2-editorial-transparency.html:344 — 'executed properly — even when you're not watching'; :716-717 FAQ — 'Cards wait for you and expire after 5 minutes if untouched — a missed card is simply no trade'; guardrail 05 (:~468) 'A signal expires after 5 minutes.'
findings.why_it_matters: The headline promise is the one thing the product structurally cannot deliver (by design — human approval is the safety feature). Buyers who came for set-and-forget churn immediately; buyers who want discipline aren't addressed by the H1. The offer is aimed at the wrong job.
findings.fix: Reframe the H1 around the real value: disciplined, instant, stop-protected execution at the moment you approve — e.g. 'One tap, and the signal is executed by the rulebook — hard stop in, profits staged, every step logged.' Sell missed-card-equals-no-trade as a guardrail, not hide it.

findings.title: Free plan promises 'the verified record' as an inclusion, and the objection line claims a live read-only feed
findings.finding: The Demo plan card lists 'the verified record' as a deliverable and the record section rebuts cherry-picking with a present-tense claim of a read-only feed. Neither exists; the record is sample data by the page's own admission.
findings.evidence: site-mockups/site-2-editorial-transparency.html:587 — 'The full pipeline on a demo account — live trade cards, the verified record, every guardrail'; :556 — '"Cherry-picked?" It's a read-only feed — we can't delete the bad trades. Verify it yourself.'
findings.why_it_matters: The free tier's flagship inclusion is a thing the buyer will never receive; the objection-handler is itself an unsubstantiated claim. Meanwhile the real deliverable — a per-trade audit ledger of the tester's own demo trades (backend/app/ledger.py, performance_ledger) — is stronger and true, and isn't mentioned in the plan card.
findings.fix: Swap 'the verified record' for 'a full audit ledger of your own demo trades — every approval, execution, TP and SL move, exportable'. Delete or future-tense the read-only-feed line until a read-only broker connection exists.

findings.title: The pricing section has plan cards but no offer ladder — nothing to pay for is defined, plus a live-trading tease and 'Cancel anytime' with nothing to cancel
findings.finding: Pilot's only stated difference from the free Demo is 'guided setup for one tester… and safety checks before any live discussion'; Signal desk lists features with no stated benefit. No tier states what would ever justify money. The reassurance line promises 'Cancel anytime' though no subscription exists, and 'before any live discussion' plants live trading as the implied next rung.
findings.evidence: site-mockups/site-2-editorial-transparency.html:590-601 (Pilot: 'Invite access… before any live discussion'; Signal desk: 'Private setup…'), :603 'Cancel anytime. No deposit bonuses…'. No price, duration, deliverable, or outcome appears on any card.
findings.why_it_matters: A page that 'asks for trust but never makes an ask' (the repo's own MESSAGE_MAP.md:83-86 diagnosis) still hasn't made one. Undifferentiated tiers also make the free demo look like the whole product, so there is no path to paid pilots. The live-discussion tease cuts against the demo-first safety position.
findings.fix: Adopt the ladder in deliverables: value each tier by hosting + concierge setup + ledger reporting (things that exist or are honestly buildable per HOSTED_VERSION_PLAN.md), delete 'before any live discussion' and 'Cancel anytime' until a subscription with terms exists.

findings.title: No signal-provider offer exists — Nick is handed a task list with zero stated benefit
findings.finding: Both Nick documents define his role purely as unpaid QA ('your only job is the screenshot flow'; 'You are only the screenshot-to-signal gatekeeper') and ask for a test checklist back. Nowhere — docs or the Signal desk plan card — is what Nick gains articulated.
findings.evidence: docs/MESSAGE_TO_NICK.md:3 — 'your only job is the screenshot flow'; docs/NICK_SCREENSHOT_PROVIDER_GUIDE.md:10-11 — 'You are only the screenshot-to-signal gatekeeper'; site-2:599 Signal desk card lists 'screenshot ingestion, command audit logs, and a performance ledger' with no provider benefit statement.
findings.why_it_matters: Nick is the only real prospective partner in the repo and the likely source of real forward-test data — the trust asset everything else depends on. If he experiences this as chores, he drifts; if he sees the ledger as an independent timestamped record of how his signals actually execute (an honest asset for his channel), he stays engaged and supplies the record.
findings.fix: Add a 5-line 'What you get' header to both Nick docs and the Signal desk card: gatekeeper control over every card, a timestamped forward-test ledger of his signals' execution, protection of his reputation from followers' bad fills, zero admin burden. See deliverables section 4.

findings.title: README declares 'no AI parsing (deterministic only)' while the shipped Nick flow requires Claude vision extraction
findings.finding: README's not-in-v1 list rules out AI parsing, but backend/app/vision_extractor.py calls the Anthropic vision API (claude-sonnet-4-5) and BEN_NEXT_STAGE_CHECKLIST.md instructs enabling SIGNAL_EXTRACTOR=claude for real screenshots. AI reads the screenshot into text; only the deterministic parser validates it — but the README's flat denial no longer matches the codebase.
findings.evidence: README.md:41 — '❌ AI / fuzzy signal parsing (deterministic only)'; backend/app/vision_extractor.py:81 DEFAULT_MODEL='claude-sonnet-4-5', :120 ANTHROPIC_URL='https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages'; docs/BEN_NEXT_STAGE_CHECKLIST.md:'SIGNAL_EXTRACTOR=claude / ANTHROPIC_API_KEY'.
findings.why_it_matters: For a product whose entire pitch is 'everything visible and logged, no black box', a checkable contradiction between the README and the code is exactly the kind of thing a skeptical trader (or Nick) will find and read as spin. The truthful version is actually a selling point: AI transcribes, a deterministic parser is the only gate, and a human provider confirms every extraction.
findings.fix: Amend README to: 'AI is used only to transcribe screenshots into text; a deterministic parser is the sole validator, and the provider must confirm every extraction before any card is sent. No AI ever creates or approves a trade.'

findings.title: FAQ setup-time claim ('usually takes about 20 minutes') is unsubstantiated and contradicts the install guide's 45 minutes
findings.finding: The FAQ asserts a guided setup 'usually takes about 20 minutes', implying an established hosted/guided onboarding track record. The only setup that exists is self-install: Python, BotFather bot creation, two terminal servers, MT5 EA compile — budgeted at 45 minutes by the repo's own guide, with hosted onboarding still a plan.
findings.evidence: site-mockups/site-2-editorial-transparency.html:717 — 'A guided setup usually takes about 20 minutes.'; INSTALL_AND_USER_GUIDE.md:46 — 'About 45 minutes and a bit of patience the first time'; HOSTED_VERSION_PLAN.md:31-33 describes today's setup as 'Six fiddly steps, several of them developer-grade.'
findings.why_it_matters: The free demo is the whole conversion engine, and its first real-world moment (setup) will take 2-3x the promised time — the classic overpromise that makes every other claim on the page suspect.
findings.fix: Either state 'setup takes about 45 minutes self-serve today; we'll walk you through it', or restructure the free demo as an operator-hosted session where the tester genuinely needs only Telegram (this already works — it is exactly how Nick onboards).

findings.title: The MT5-always-on requirement (and its ~$8-15/mo VPS cost) is absent from the site despite the plan calling it 'sales honesty'
findings.finding: For execution to happen after approval, the customer's MetaTrader must be running; HOSTED_VERSION_PLAN explicitly says the customer typically needs a forex VPS and that this 'belongs in your sales honesty'. The site's FAQ, pricing, and 'What do I need to start?' never mention it.
findings.evidence: HOSTED_VERSION_PLAN.md:60-65 — 'their MetaTrader needs to be running 24/7… commonly ~$8-15/month… it belongs in your sales honesty.'; site-2:714-717 'What do I need to start?' answer lists only 'A Telegram account and MetaTrader 5 on a demo account.'
findings.why_it_matters: For a demo it's tolerable (a sleeping laptop just means missed cards), but the moment a pilot is paid, an undisclosed recurring third-party cost is a refund-request and trust problem. Disclosing it also strengthens the Pilot tier: 'we help you set up MT5 hosting' is a legitimate paid inclusion.
findings.fix: Add one FAQ line ('MetaTrader must be running to execute; for always-on execution most traders use ~$10/mo MT5 hosting — we help set it up in the Pilot') and fold VPS setup into the Pilot tier deliverables.

findings.title: Site implies any signal/any symbol; v1 parses only XAUUSD/GOLD/XAU — undisclosed scope that should be owned as a focus feature
findings.finding: Hero and step copy say 'the signals you follow' / 'each signal from your channel' with no symbol restriction, but the parser rejects any symbol other than gold aliases.
findings.evidence: site-mockups/site-2-editorial-transparency.html:344-345 — 'The signals you follow… each signal from your channel'; backend/app/parser.py:17-20 SYMBOL_ALIASES maps only GOLD/XAU/XAUUSD, :98 rejects 'No recognised symbol (expected GOLD/XAU/XAUUSD)'.
findings.why_it_matters: An FX/indices signal-follower signs up and their very first card is rejected. Meanwhile 'gold-only pilot' is a credible discipline story ('one instrument, one rulebook, proven before expanding') rather than a limitation to hide — narrow scope stated plainly is on-brand for this positioning.
findings.fix: Add 'v1 pilot: XAUUSD (gold) signals only — more symbols after the forward-test' to the hero chip or guardrails section and to the Demo plan card.

findings.title: Demo request form has no fulfillment path and leaks mockup language to prospects
findings.finding: Submissions append to a local JSONL via the preview server, and the on-page aside tells the prospect 'Request details are saved locally when served through the included preview server' — developer language inside buyer-facing copy, with no route to an inbox or follow-up.
findings.evidence: site-mockups/site-2-editorial-transparency.html:619 — 'Request details are saved locally when served through the included preview server.'; orchestrator-verified: POST /api/demo-requests appends to site-mockups/demo-requests.jsonl.
findings.why_it_matters: Fine for a mockup; a dead end the moment a real prospect submits. A production CRM is rightly out of scope (Not built yet / outside current v1 scope — should be built minimally later), but the mockup sentence should not survive into anything a prospect sees, and the reference-code flow needs a stated 'we reply within X' promise the operator can keep manually.
findings.fix: Replace the aside line with 'We reply personally within 2 working days with your setup slot', and wire the JSONL to a daily manual check (or simple email forward) before showing the page publicly.

result.deliverables:
# SignalGate — Offer Architecture (Expert 2)

## 1. The offer ladder (named tiers)

| Tier | Name | Price | Who | Core deliverable |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | **Watch It Work** | Free, 15-min session | Any curious prospect | Operator-hosted live walkthrough: a real signal becomes a card, they tap Approve on their own phone, watch the demo execution + ledger fill in real time. Needs only Telegram. |
| 1 | **Demo Desk** | Free, 14 days | Signal-followers ready to test | A seat on operator-hosted infra + their own MT5 **demo** via the EA. Ends with their personal **Discipline Report**: exported ledger of every card, tap, fill, TP/SL move. |
| 2 | **Pilot Seat** | Paid (price TBD after trust assets), invite-only | Demo Desk graduates | Hosted seat + license key, concierge MT5-demo + optional MT5-VPS setup, weekly ledger review with the operator, priority support, pause-anytime. Still demo-only. |
| 3 | **Provider Desk** | Private setup fee or rev-share (later) | Signal providers (Nick) | Screenshot-gatekeeper ingestion, multi-tester cards, and a timestamped forward-test ledger of *their* signals' execution, exportable. |

The buyer pays for **hosting, concierge onboarding, and reporting** — never for signals, never for expected profit. Everything in tiers 0-1 exists today (the Nick flow proves the hosted pattern); tier 2 requires HOSTED_VERSION_PLAN steps 1-4.

## 2. The free demo offer (rewrite)

> **See a signal become a disciplined trade — in 15 minutes, on your phone.**
> Book a live demo. You need only Telegram. A real gold signal arrives as a structured card; you tap Approve; it executes on a demo account with a hard stop and staged take-profits, and you watch the audit ledger record every step as it happens. No install. No card. Nothing at risk. v1 is XAUUSD-only and demo-only, on purpose.

What makes it irresistible without overpromising: the **live audit trail** is the spectacle — buyers in this category have never seen a signal product show its own ledger filling in. Do not promise returns, away-from-screen execution, or any-symbol support. The CTA microcopy stays: "One tap to approve, one to ignore."

## 3. The paid pilot offer (what justifies money later)

**Pilot Seat — demo-only, by invitation, after your 14-day Demo Desk.**
Included: (1) hosted backend + shared bot (no Python, no BotFather, no terminals); (2) personal license key tied to your seat; (3) guided MT5 demo-EA setup, plus MT5-VPS setup help if you want always-on execution (~$10/mo third-party cost, disclosed up front); (4) weekly 20-minute ledger review — what you approved, what you ignored, where your fills landed vs the signal; (5) direct line to the operator; (6) leave anytime and keep your full ledger export.
Explicitly excluded, in writing: live trading, auto-copy, profit expectations. Price is set **only after** the trust assets in §5 exist; until then the card reads "Invite access — pricing published after the forward-test record."

## 4. The signal-provider offer (Nick)

Lead both Nick docs and the Provider Desk card with what he *gets*, not his task list:
1. **Gatekeeper control** — nothing goes to testers unless he confirms every number; AI only transcribes, the deterministic parser validates, he approves.
2. **An independent forward-test record of his signals** — timestamped, warts-included, execution-level. This is an asset no screenshot-posting competitor has, and the only honest performance proof he can ever show his channel.
3. **Reputation protection** — his followers stop executing his calls badly (late fills, moved stops) and blaming the signal.
4. **Zero admin burden** — no pause/logs/servers; two minutes per signal.
The ask: two weeks of real screenshots + the existing test checklist. Later commercial shape: Provider Desk fee, or SignalGate as the "verified execution layer" he offers his subscribers.

## 5. Trust assets required before taking any money

1. **A real forward-test record**: 1-3 months of actual demo trades from the ledger (Nick's signals), published with losses, replacing every SAMPLE figure and the fabricated 168-trade/+8.1% chart.
2. **A genuine read-only verification path** (MT5 investor-password / read-only feed) matching the "read-only" copy — or that copy is deleted.
3. **Named operator, contact channel, honest regulatory line** (fill copy-deck §7 placeholders; keep the "not authorised as a financial adviser — forward-testing and education" framing).
4. **Hosted deployment live** (VPS, HTTPS, license keys, 2-3 friendly testers onboarded end-to-end per HOSTED_VERSION_PLAN §"Suggested order").
5. **Legal/financial-promotion review** — the plan itself calls this the biggest non-technical risk.
6. **Working request fulfillment** — form submissions reach a real inbox with a kept reply-time promise.
7. **Written cancel/refund terms** — before "Cancel anytime" appears anywhere.

## 6. Remove — it weakens the offer

- FAQ sentence "…is independently reconciled" (site-2:700) — unqualified fabricated verification.
- "It's a read-only feed — we can't delete the bad trades" (:556) — claims infrastructure that doesn't exist.
- "the verified record" as a Demo-plan inclusion (:587) → replace with "full audit ledger of your own demo trades, exportable".
- Hero clause "even when you're not watching" (:344) — structurally undeliverable; replace with the discipline framing.
- Step 1 "SignalGate reads it the moment it lands" (:409) — no channel ingestion exists.
- "A guided setup usually takes about 20 minutes" (:717) — no guided setup has ever run; guide says 45 min.
- "before any live discussion" in the Pilot card (:593) — a live-trading tease that undercuts the demo-first position.
- "Cancel anytime" (:603) — nothing to cancel yet.
- The sample equity curve **in the hero** (:358-382). Even labelled SAMPLE, a made-up performance chart as the page's opening image is the category's #1 scam pattern. Move performance proof to the record section only; put a real trade-card + ledger screenshot in the hero — product proof, not performance proof.
- Mockup plumbing sentence "saved locally when served through the included preview server" (:619) from buyer-facing copy.
